In the United States, women gained the national right to vote with the ratification of the 19th Amendment on August 18, 1920, certified on August 26, 1920 [d1, d5, d8]. However, women's suffrage was achieved at different times in various states and localities before 1920 [d3, d6], and full enfranchisement for all women took additional decades [d5]. Globally, many nations granted women the vote at different times; for example, British women over 30 gained the vote in 1918, Dutch women in 1919, and French women in 1944 [d2], with at least 20 countries preceding the U.S. [d10].
